title.ja: 改正鮮明廣島市實測地圖
title.en: Revised Clear Survey Map of Hiroshima City, 1896

description.ja:
明治29年（1896）10月に広島で刊行された、折りたたみ式の広島市街図。十月十日印刷、同月二十日発行。著作兼発行者は広島市大手町二丁目の早速有、印刷人は大阪の大石栄吉、大賣捌所は同じ大手町二丁目の早速社で、表紙に「廣島　早速社發兌」とある。
一枚の紙に三図を収める。主図の「改正鮮明廣島市實測地圖」は、図上に「日本里程一万六千分之一」と刻み、町を単位とする縮尺棒を添える。これに「廣島附近交通之圖」と「宮島ノ圖」が伴う。主図は「符合」と題した凡例を備え、國縣道・道・堀・川・堤・鉄道を線種で、官衙を●、會社を×、學校を「文」の記号で描き分ける。町名・橋名・寺社を稠密に注記し、縣廳・縣會議事堂・市役所・控訴院・郵便電信局・廣島中學校・尋常師範學校などを記す。広島城の本丸は図中で唯一朱に塗られ、「師團本營」と読める四字を入れ、その周囲に步兵營・砲兵營・工兵方面・火薬庫・射的場・陸軍監獄・西練兵場・東練兵場を配する。市街北東には「停車場」（「廣島驛」の表記はとらない）を置き、そこから南に鉄道が延びて宇品町の埠頭に至る。図中には「停車場及哩數」（哩・鎖）、「諸街道里程」（里・丁・間）、「宇品ヨリ海上里程」の三表を備え、鉄道はマイル法、街道は尺貫法という当時の併用状況をそのまま示す。全体は55×40cm、折りたたむと14cm、内匡は48×37cm。
裏面には「廣島縣巡遊指南車」（探勝僊史編述）を十五丁にわたって刷る。表題はこれを「附」として掲げる。内容は名所案内ではなく、県内二十二郡を順に扱う実用的な地誌である。県域の四至と面積、町村数・戸数・人口といった統計を掲げたうえで、広島市の項では河川・港湾・官公署・学校・銀行・工場を列挙し、以下、沼田郡から豊田郡まで郡ごとに中心町、郡役所・警察署・裁判所の有無、街道と駅、河川・山岳、名産を一、二行ずつ記す。厳島は佐伯郡の項で「日本三景の一なり」と特筆される。宇品は軍港としてではなく、船舶の出入りで賑わう商港として記述される。
日清戦争への言及は、この案内記の序文冒頭にのみ現れる。序文は広島を「中國の咽喉」と位置づけ、明治二十七・二十八両年の役に際して天皇の大本営が置かれ、駐在が数か月に及び、数万の兵が集まったこと、凱旋後も市街の繁華が以前の比ではないことを述べ、それゆえ全国の人々がこの地を詳しく知る必要がある、それがこの地図と一篇を著した理由である、と刊行の趣意を結ぶ。約260字の序文のうち戦争に触れるのは約75字で、二丁以降にこの主題は戻らない。一方、主図の側に戦争そのものへの言及はなく、そこに定着しているのは平時の常設の師団駐屯地としての姿である（案内記本文も広島市の項で、旧城趾に第五師團と第九旅團が置かれ軍營となっている旨を記す）。刊行はこの戦争の終結から約一年半後にあたる。
刊行元の早速社は、広島の実業家早速勝三（1847-1918）が明治15年（1882）に書籍取次販売業として起こしたもので、勝三はのち芸備日日新聞の社主となった。国立国会図書館の書誌によれば、早速社は法令書・教科書を主力としつつ、勝三自身の著作として『広島県庁・鎮台・裁判職員録』（1884）、『広島県職員録』（1889）、『広島県新旧市町村名全書』（1889）といった県内の実用書を刊行し、明治20年代に入ると『伊都岐島八景』（1892）、『広島市内名所一覧表』（1894）を出している。この二点はいずれも本図と同じ早速有の著作であり、本図はその系譜に連なる。早速有と勝三との血縁関係は、参照した書誌類からは確認できなかった。
なお本図と同時期の広島には、清水庫三郎『改正實測廣島市街全圖』（1893、1894）、和田信『廣島市街全圖 : 實測最新』（1894）など複数の市街図が刊行されている。本図を主題として論じた研究は、国立国会図書館サーチ、CiNii Books、CiNii Researchの検索では確認できなかった。CiNii Booksに登録された所蔵機関は国際日本文化研究センターの1館のみである。

description.en:
A folding street map of Hiroshima, published there in October 1896: printed on the 10th and published on the 20th. The author-publisher was 早速有 (Hayami Tamotsu?) of 59 Ōtemachi 2-chōme, Hiroshima; the printer was 大石栄吉 (Ōishi Eikichi?) of Osaka; the principal distributor was Hayami-sha, on the same street, and the cover reads "Hiroshima: Published by Hayami-sha."
A single sheet carries three maps. The principal map is inscribed 日本里程一万六千分之一 — one part in 16,000 of Japanese linear measure — with a bar scale graduated in chō; it is accompanied by a "Map of Transportation in the Vicinity of Hiroshima" and a "Map of Miyajima." A key headed 符合 distinguishes prefectural and national roads, lesser roads, moats, rivers, embankments and railway by line type, and marks government offices, companies and schools by symbol. Street and bridge names and temples and shrines are densely annotated, and the prefectural office, prefectural assembly hall, city hall, court of appeal, post and telegraph office and the middle and normal schools are all named. The keep enclosure of Hiroshima Castle is the only block printed in red, lettered as the divisional headquarters, and around it stand the infantry and artillery barracks, the engineers' directorate, a powder magazine, a rifle range, the army prison and the eastern and western parade grounds. To the north-east the sheet marks simply "the station" — it does not use the form "Hiroshima Station" — and a railway runs south from it to the wharves at Ujina. Three tables appear on the face: railway distances by station in miles and chains, road distances in ri, chō and ken, and sea distances from Ujina to Itsukushima, Kure, Mitsuhama, Onomichi, Okayama, Shimonoseki and Yokohama — the imperial and the traditional systems side by side, as they then were. The sheet measures 55 × 40 cm and folds to 14 cm; the neatline measures 48 × 37 cm.
The verso carries "A Guide to Touring Hiroshima Prefecture," compiled by 探勝僊史 (Tanshō Senshi?), across fifteen folios, advertised on the title panel as an appendix to the map. It is not a guide to famous places but a working gazetteer of the prefecture's twenty-two districts. After the prefecture's bounds, area, and counts of towns, villages, households and population, the section on Hiroshima City lists its rivers, harbours, government offices, schools, banks and factories; thereafter each district in turn receives a line or two on its chief town, whether it has a district office, police station or court, its highways and post stations, its rivers and mountains, and its products. Itsukushima is singled out, under Saeki district, as one of the three great views of Japan. Ujina is described not as a military port but as a commercial one, busy with the coming and going of ships.
The Sino-Japanese War appears only in the guide's opening paragraph. There Hiroshima is called the throat of the Chūgoku region, and the author recalls that in the campaign of 1894-95 the emperor's headquarters were established in the city, that the imperial residence there ran to several months, that tens of thousands of troops assembled, and that even after the triumphal return the city's prosperity bore no comparison with former days — from which he concludes that people throughout Japan need to know the place in detail, and that this is why the map and the essay were written. Of roughly 260 characters of preface, some seventy-five concern the war, and the subject does not return after the first folio. The map itself names no war: what is fixed on it is the peacetime garrison, the standing divisional headquarters returned to the castle grounds. Publication came about a year and a half after the war ended.
Hayami-sha was founded in 1882 as a book wholesaling and retail business by the Hiroshima entrepreneur Hayami Katsuzō (1847-1918), who later became proprietor of the newspaper Geibi Nichinichi Shinbun. National Diet Library records show the firm publishing chiefly law books and textbooks, alongside practical works for the prefecture written by Katsuzō himself — directories of the prefectural office, garrison and courts (1884), of prefectural staff (1889), and a concordance of old and new municipal names (1889) — and, from the 1890s, Itsukishima hakkei (1892) and a list of noted places within Hiroshima City (1894). Both of the latter are credited to 早速有, the same hand as this map, and the map belongs with them. Any family relationship between him and Katsuzō could not be established from the catalogue records consulted.
Several other street maps of Hiroshima were published in the same years, among them Shimizu Kurasaburō's Kaisei jissoku Hiroshima shigai zenzu (1893, 1894) and Wada Shin's Hiroshima shigai zenzu: jissoku saishin (1894). No study devoted to this particular sheet was found in searches of NDL Search, CiNii Books or CiNii Research. The only holding institution registered in CiNii Books is Nichibunken.

  • Title: Kaisei senmei Hiroshima-shi jissoku chizu 改正鮮明廣島市實測地圖 [Revised, Clearly Printed Actual-Survey Map of Hiroshima City], revised October 1896
  • Inner titles: the survey map of Hiroshima City; "Map of Transportation in the Vicinity of Hiroshima" (廣島附近交通之圖); "Map of Miyajima" (宮島ノ圖)
  • Title panel: 明治二十九年十月改正　改正鮮明　廣島市實測地圖　附　廣島縣巡遊指南車 — "Revised October 1896: Revised, Clearly Printed Actual-Survey Map of Hiroshima City, with A Guide to Touring Hiroshima Prefecture"
  • Cover title (as recorded by the Nichibunken OPAC): 廣島市實測地圖 : 改正鮮明. The cover itself carries the full title-panel text.
  • Cover inscription: "Hiroshima: Published by Hayami-sha" (廣島　早速社發兌)
  • Author and publisher: 早速有, of 59 Ōtemachi 2-chōme, Hiroshima. The reading of the given name is unsettled — NDL records both Hayami Tamotsu and Sassoku Ari; the Nichibunken catalogue records no reading.
  • Printer: 大石栄吉 (Ōishi Eikichi — reading inferred, unattested), Minami-ku, Osaka
  • Principal distributor: Hayami-sha (早速社), Ōtemachi 2-chōme, Hiroshima
  • Printed 10 October 1896; published 20 October 1896
  • One sheet bearing three maps; 55 × 40 cm, folding to 14 cm; neatline 48 × 37 cm
  • Scale: 1:16,000. The sheet itself is inscribed 日本里程一万六千分之一 — one part in 16,000 of Japanese linear measure — with a bar scale graduated in chō.
  • Tables on the face: railway distances by station in miles and chains (停車場及哩數); road distances in ri, chō and ken (諸街道里程); sea distances from Ujina (宇品ヨリ海上里程) to Itsukushima, Kure, Mitsuhama, Onomichi, Okayama, Shimonoseki and Yokohama
  • Verso: "A Guide to Touring Hiroshima Prefecture" (廣島縣巡遊指南車), compiled by 探勝僊史 (Tanshō Senshi — reading inferred, unattested); fifteen folios, no colophon
  • Provenance: unknown. Held by: International Research Center for Japanese Studies (Nichibunken), Kyoto
